title: Okanagan
sub: Okanagan Lake 08NM083 · Penticton 08NM050 · Oliver 08NM085 · Summerland CS · Wells Dam
blurb: A drought year on the lake, which rose only 0.7 m, that was also the biggest sockeye return in ten years of Wells Dam counts: 491,039 fish.
name: okanagan_wy2024

lanes.label: Okanagan Lake level, Kelowna
lanes.does: A low F held under everything, louder as the lake fills; cello adds a 5th while it rises.

lanes.label: Lake vs. 15-yr normal
lanes.does: Sets the harmony's brightness: below normal leans one mode darker.

lanes.label: Outflow at Penticton dam
lanes.does: Piano density follows the release. When the dam holds the flow flat, the piano plays strictly, with no variation.

lanes.label: Okanagan River near Oliver
lanes.does: Soft log drums, conga and shaker.

lanes.label: Sockeye passing Wells Dam
lanes.does: Marimba runs climb the chord; more fish means more notes, and the runs start higher as the season goes.

lanes.label: Water temperature at Wells
lanes.does: Above 18 C a violin holds a high note: thermal stress for migrating sockeye.

lanes.label: Sockeye spawning near Oliver
lanes.does: Low, falling cello pizzicato around mid-October, scaled by run size. Timing is modelled.

lanes.label: Rain
lanes.does: Harp notes from the current chord. Rain vs. snow is split by temperature.

lanes.label: Humidity (daily min)
lanes.does: Humid days get a long hall reverb; dry days a short, bright room.

events: Early Oct: sandhill cranes passing over (typical timing)
Oct 2023: the 2023 sockeye spawning near Oliver (timing simulated) - low cello pizzicato
Outflow held flat by the dam (Oct 01) - piano turns strict
Green-up: string pad enters (Mar 14; MODIS MOD17A2HGF)
First sockeye of the 2024 run pass Wells Dam (May 29) - marimba
Lake peaks at gauge 2.04 m (Jul 04); 2017 reached 3.01
Sockeye peak at Wells: 29,931 fish in one day (Jul 11)
Wells water passes 18 C (Aug 04) - held high violin: thermal stress
Okanagan River at Oliver peaks, 28 m3/s (Aug 31) - fullest percussion
